passages.provision_quote: Beginning in 2026, aT ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL:
passages.note: The bill amends seventeen statute sections covering polling places, sample ballots, early ballot requests, signature verification, canvass deadlines and recounts, and its identification clause is optional rather than required.

rows.reasoning: Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted Aye on HB2785 (2024), an omnibus election bill whose identification clause is permissive rather than mandatory: "THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT". That leans toward identification-based verification but establishes neither "Require photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot" nor "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote", and the bill leaves signature verification as the default route. The House vote was "Passed 56-2-0-0-2", near-unanimous, so it cannot carry a chair on its own either.
